This was a same-day (immediate) booking cancelled 9 min 0 s after matching (F4), i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so on the face of NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable and no automatic refund is available to the rider.

Ryde's own published position is that the $6.61 is a fee-waiver request submitted via RydeHELP within 30 days of the trip and refunded as a voucher, and the rider filed this dispute within days of the 09:09:10 cancellation on the same trip (F4); there is no evidence the 30-day window was missed, so the request is not time-barred.

The rider has 3 prior disputes in 90 days, none upheld, and the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F17, F18), so neither profile supports any account-level action against the other party; profile facts cannot decide this case in any event.

Nothing in the chat, the complaint or the driver's statement contains a threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F9–F13), and the trip records show no incident (F15, F16), so no safety escalation applies on this record.

The traffic records for the trip window show only a moderate speed band on Anson Road (band 4, 30–39 km/h, F14) and no incidents at all (F15) under fair weather (F16); no congestion, incident or road-closure reason exists to explain any unmet expectation of the rider or to excuse either party.

Profile facts cut against the rider, not for her: F17 shows 3 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld, versus the driver's clean record (F18), which the other side will cite to argue this is a repeat fee-grumbling pattern — though profile facts cannot decide the case.

The rider cancelled at 09:09:10, 9 minutes after acceptance and 6 min 30 s after the platform-recorded arrival at 09:02:40 — a rider-side cancellation after the driver had already arrived and waited, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is properly chargeable and NS-2 does not apply because no NS-1 element failed.

The rider's own message at 09:05 asked for "2 more minutes" and no further message ever announced her arrival, while the driver's 09:08 message records two unanswered calls after 5 minutes of waiting; the chat record is complete with all three messages timestamped, so nothing in it contradicts the GPS wait.
